Alicante (aka Alacant/both are official city names) is a port city in Spain on Costa Blanca, as well as the capital of Alicante Province and of Alacanti comarca. Alicante is also a major Mediterranean port (cargo and ferry), with city population around 330,000. By population (around 760,000), Alicante Metro is ranked Spain's 8th-largest.

By annual passenger shipping traffic, Alicante is one of Spain's major ports (for both cruise vessels and ferries), with more than 70 calls/visits by cruise ships and estimated 100,000+ passengers plus 40,000+ crew annually. Studies show that the average expenditure per cruise tourist is EUR 300+, including expenses on hotels, shopping, and excursions (before/after the voyage).

Port Alicante (locode ESALC) serves regularly scheduled ferry connections linking Spain with Algeria (Oran, Algiers, Mostaganem) and the Balearic Islands (Mallorca), the latter route being operated from Denia (to the northeast of Alicante).

In December 2022, Global Ports Holding (UK-based cruise port operator company/currently ranked the world's largest) announced winning the public tender and being awarded by the Alicante Port Authority a 15-year concession of Alicante Cruise Port (2023 thru 2038). The facility is operated via a joint venture consortium (80:20) between Global Ports Holding and Sepcan SL Maritime (Servicios Portuarios Canarios). The port concession deal was signed in March 2023.

In 2023, the Port reported a record year with scheduled 86 cruise ship calls and estimated 200,000+ tourists. The booked berthings included both stopovers and homeporting (embarkation/debarkation). In 2023, MSC Cruises increased/doubled its homeport operations by basing here two liners (MSC Lirica, MSC Orchestra) for a total of 25 roundtrip voyages out of Alicante. Of the 86 visits, 7 were maiden - by cruise ships making their inaugural calls in Alicante.

Among the city's most notable features are Castell de Santa Barbara (9th-century castle on Mt Benacantil, overlooking the city) and the Port. The latter was a subject of controversy in 2006–2007 as the residents successfully battled to keep it from being changed into an industrial estate. Santa Barbara Castle's La Torreta Tower is its oldest part, while the walls and part of the lowest zone were constructed during the 18th century.

The promenade Explanada de Espana is lined by palm trees and paved with 6.5M marble floor tiles that create a wavy form. The Promenade is one of the most beautiful promenades in Spain and extends from Port of Alicante to Gran Vía, ending at the statue of Mark Hersch. For Alicante's residents, Explanada de Espana is the meeting place for traditional Spanish paseo, or evening stroll along the waterfront, and a venue for musical concerts. At its end is a monument by the artist Banuls of the 19th century.

Just a few kilometers from the city is Tabarca Island. Once a haven for Barbary pirates, today it is a beautiful tourist attraction.

At a Glance

Easy independently. Cruise ships dock at Alicante Cruise Terminal, about 1 km (0.6 mi) from the city center. Alicante’s waterfront, historic center, Santa Bárbara Castle and Postiguet Beach are all close enough to combine during a typical port call.

Getting from the Cruise Port

Ships normally berth at the outer Levante piers. The exact walking distance depends on the berth, but passengers can usually reach the marina and city waterfront in about 15–25 minutes.

A port shuttle generally operates between the cruise terminal and the waterfront near the city center. Service arrangements can vary by call, so confirm the drop-off point and final return time onboard. Taxis may also be available at the terminal.

From the waterfront, the Explanada de España, old town and Postiguet Beach are readily accessible on foot. Alicante’s buses and TRAM are more useful for beaches and neighborhoods outside the center than for the main central sights.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Old Town and Waterfront

Allow 2–3 hours for the Explanada de España, Town Hall area, San Nicolás Co-Cathedral, Santa María Basilica and the narrow streets of the historic center. Most of this area is compact and pedestrian-friendly, although the Santa Cruz neighborhood contains steep lanes and steps.

Santa Bárbara Castle

Allow about 2–3 hours including access and sightseeing. The castle stands above the city on Mount Benacantil and offers broad views over Alicante and the coast.

The easiest approach is via the lift entrance on Avenida Juan Bautista Lafora, opposite Postiguet Beach, or by the castle minibus when operating. Walking to the summit is possible but involves a sustained uphill climb, uneven surfaces and steps. Check current lift or minibus operation before setting out.

Postiguet Beach

This central urban beach lies beside the old town and below the castle, making it practical for a short swim or a relaxed waterfront stop. Allow 1–3 hours. It is much easier to combine with sightseeing than the more distant beaches along the coast.

Museums and Local Culture

The Contemporary Art Museum of Alicante is close to Santa María Basilica, while the archaeological museum, MARQ, is farther north of the old town. The Ocean Race Museum is particularly convenient near the marina and can fit into a shorter call. Verify opening days and admission arrangements before relying on a museum visit.

Tabarca Island

Boats from Alicante generally take about one hour each way. A visit usually requires around 6 hours including the crossings, so it is suitable only for a long port call with well-matched seasonal boat times. Because departures can be limited and sea conditions may affect service, this is less reliable than staying in Alicante.

Self-Guided Walking Tours

Easy Waterfront and Old Town Walk

Distance: approximately 3 km (1.9 mi). Pure walking time: about 45 minutes. Recommended total time: 2–3 hours. Difficulty: easy, mostly level.

  1. Start at the port shuttle stop or marina entrance.
  2. Walk along the palm-lined Explanada de España.
  3. Continue to Alicante Town Hall and the surrounding old-town streets.
  4. Visit San Nicolás Co-Cathedral.
  5. Walk to Santa María Basilica and the nearby Contemporary Art Museum.
  6. Continue to Postiguet Beach.
  7. Return along the waterfront to the shuttle stop or port entrance.

This route is suitable for most visitors. Cobblestones and short inclines occur within the old town, but the waterfront sections are largely flat.

Castle and Santa Cruz Walk

Distance: approximately 5 km (3.1 mi), excluding any shuttle ride from the berth. Pure walking time: about 1 hour 30 minutes. Recommended total time: 3–4 hours. Difficulty: moderate to challenging, with steep lanes and many steps.

  1. Start at the marina and walk beside Postiguet Beach.
  2. Use the castle lift if operating, or climb by a signed pedestrian route.
  3. Explore Santa Bárbara Castle and its viewpoints.
  4. Descend through La Ereta Park.
  5. Continue through the hillside Santa Cruz neighborhood.
  6. Visit Santa María Basilica and the Town Hall area.
  7. Return via the Explanada de España.

The Santa Cruz section is accessible only on foot and is unsuitable for some visitors with limited mobility. Using the lift for the ascent reduces the effort but does not remove the steep descent, steps and uneven paving.

Trips Beyond Alicante

Excursions may visit Elche and its historic palm groves, coastal towns or inland villages. These destinations require road or rail transport and leave less time for Alicante itself. An organized excursion is preferable when the itinerary includes several distant stops or when the port call is short.

San Juan Beach can be reached independently by TRAM or bus, but the extra travel is rarely necessary for passengers who only want a brief beach visit because Postiguet Beach is beside the city center.

Practical Tips

  • Confirm the shuttle’s final departure time before leaving the port area.
  • Allow additional time if your berth is at the far end of the cruise pier.
  • Wear suitable footwear for Santa Cruz and the castle approaches.
  • Carry sun protection and water, especially when climbing Mount Benacantil.
  • Check current museum, castle lift, boat and public-transport schedules locally.
  • Leave a generous return margin for shuttle queues, traffic and terminal procedures.
